original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 54 Mbaud DVB-S2 and 5G NR demodulator on a low-end Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) or Central Processing Unit (CPU).Targeted Improvements: Enabling a 54 Mbaud software defined radio for low end platforms not existing today in ESA Member States.Description: Previous projects have demonstrated that carriers of equivalent bandwidth can be demodulated in software on x86 server-level CPUs. Also, by using high-performance GPUs and parallel processing, bandwidths of hundreds of MHz or even many GHz could be demodulated. To date, a low-cost GPU or CPU-based demodulation solution with typical consumer terminal performance have not been developed. Such technology would allow field-upgradable terminals that can enable the deployment of new waveforms without expensive hardware swaps in the middle of the life of the system.This activity will develop and test a software-based demodulator running in a consumer GPU as found in a games console or a PC graphics card or a low-end CPU (Intel Core i3 or equivalent), with a throughput equivalent to a TV receiver or a consumer satellite broadband terminal. Superior demodulation algorithms than those in common open-source Software Defined Radio (SDR) toolkits will be studied and further developed and implemented.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall implement and test a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on one of the hardware platforms described above. The DVB-S2/X demodulator software will be tested against a hardware modulator or dedicated test equipment in the relevant environment to ensure the baud rate is met and fully compliant with as a minimum theDVB-S2 specification. Phase 1 deliverable will be a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on a low-end CPU or GPU platform. Budget is up to 700 kEuro.- Phase 2 shall implement and test in the relevant environment 5G-NR waveform or other proprietary waveform development on the hardware platform delivered by Phase 1.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: Objective: To develop a proof-of-concept of a modular robust waveform for E2E communications that offers further protection for the missions, in a modular approach in accordance with the mission security needs.Description:Intentional RF interference is a threat to space missions, as it can disrupt the radio links between satellite and ground/users. There are waveform techniques that can counter or mitigate the impact of that interference but they need to be designed specifically against reference threats. This activity is aimed at developing a modular robust waveform for end-to-end (E2E) communications offering further protection for the missions, by designing the waveform aspects as well as the receiver operations. It will consider typical RF threats and tune the waveform against the most common ones, so that space missions do not have to develop new solutions for their case. The design of the modular robust waveform can include cryptographically robust spread sequences that can be used to drive a frequency hopping scheme, or a direct Sequence spread spectrum modulation, coupled with Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM). The adaptation algorithm of the ACM can cover both the typical Modulation and Coding schemes as well as the Transmission Security (TRANSEC) functions (e.g. Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum and Frequency Hopping), providing flexible level of protection based on the link conditions. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the most common RF interference signals and attacks method - Investigation of state of theart signal techniques to counter RF interference and development of a SWAT analysis to select the optimum measures for the consolidated attacks options. - Detailed design of the waveform blocks to counter the identified common RF interference threats. Particular emphasis shall be devoted to the Add-on modularity so that each block can be added as plug-in. - Development of a Proof of Concept simulator including signal generator/receiver of the waveform and assessment of the E2E performance of the proposed Waveform. - Investigation of the regulatory constraints from the Radio Frequency Compatibility with specific focus on the impact of wideband signals on ITU frequency bands allocation. The software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, Software

original.description: This activity supports the evolution of European large (> 1 ton) LEO satellite platforms in line with ESA's Zero Debris objective by 2030. Building on previous work performed with European system integrators, it will mature platform designs from System Requirements Review (SRR) to Preliminary Design Review (PDR) level while advancing key Zero Debris technologies towards operational readiness.The activity will address end-of-life disposal, resilience against failures, health monitoring, and preparation for removal throughthe development and integration of innovative platform technologies. It will combine system-level platform design activities with technology maturation and co-engineering between platform integrators and specialised technology suppliers. The overall objective isto enable the next generation of European satellite product lines, supporting the implementation of the Space Debris Mitigation policy while maintaining technical feasibility, competitiveness, and affordability.

original.description: Objective:To develop and validate an AI-based assistant for interactive access, querying and assisted manipulation of SysML v2 space system models to reduce modelling effort and increase design quality.Description:Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) is an approach to manage the complexity of future space systems.Working effectively with large digital models is challenging; understanding structure and dependencies,reusing assets across projects, and extracting decision-relevant information is time-consuming andexpert-dependent.Limited and non-intuitive access to very large models slows MBSE adoption and reduces the return oninvestments, especially in early phases where it drives duplication, and late inconsistency discovery causeshigher design risk. SysML v2 introduces combined textual and graphical modelling with a standardised API for programmatic access, which lowers the access barrier. AI - and particularly Large Language Models (LLMs) - can help translate user intent into controlled, explainable interactions with these formal SysML v2 models, overcoming the barriers identified.This activity will develop an AI assistant that acts as an intermediate layer between users and formal modelsand operates exclusively via the SysML v2 textual notation and standard API. It will support (i) natural-language assistance for incremental model creation and modification, (ii) model querying and automated consistency checking, (iii) guided exploration of dependencies, (iv) identification and extraction of reusable model elements, and (v) structured summarization of model content for expert and non-expert stakeholders. The focus is on human assistance, incremental model generation and knowledge exploitation that helps system engineerswork with large system models - not on autonomous end-to-end model generation or mission-specifictoolchains.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of SysML v2 capabilities, APIs, and relevant AI techniques for model creation and interaction- Identification of representative use cases for querying, exploration, and reuse of SysML v2 models- Definition of a reference architecture ensuring controlled AI interaction via the SysML v2 API- Development of proof-of-concept AI components for model generation, querying and summarization- Validation of the approach on representative SysML v2 models, using the ESA MBSE methodology- Assessment of benefits, limitations, and roadmap towards higher TRL.The activity will result in validated concepts, software prototypes, and documented lessons learned, enablingfollow-on developments under GSTP or other programmes focusing on operational deployment.Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entitieswithin ESA Member States can access it and can provide update to the community of users.
